title: Evidence conflict resolution — v1.0
description: plan.md §11, gate table row G11: 'unresolved evidence conflict' blocks promotion -- only unresolved conflicts block, per chainlink #20's own description. One per specs/_conflicts/<conflict_id>.json -- workspace-level, matching evidence/'s own scope (conflicts arise between evidence records, which aren't owned by any one crate; the promotion-receipt worked example in §7 lists evidence/E-0143.json and specs/_conflicts/EC-004.json as siblings with no crate prefix, unlike boundary/interaction artifact_manifest entries which do carry one). status is the field G11 checks directly: 'resolved' requires resolution + review (enforced by this schema's own if/then, the same conditional-requirement pattern plan.md §1.1 already uses for mode: port requiring port_source); 'unresolved' has neither yet, since there is no selected authority or human sign-off before resolution. This IS in plan.md §7.2's human-checkpoint list ('evidence-conflict resolution'), unlike bare evidence records, so it carries a review block and IS routed through pipeline.py's approve().

conflict_id.description: Must equal the filename stem exactly (G1b, enforced by scripts/validate_conflict_resolution.py).

evidence.description: The two conflicting evidence ids. plan.md §11's worked example and `resolution.disposition_of_other` (singular) both model a pairwise conflict -- exactly one winner, one loser; a three-or-more-evidence conflict would leave `disposition_of_other` unable to say which loser it describes, so it is rejected here rather than silently accepted with an ambiguous resolution.

selected_authority.description: Must be one of the ids listed in this record's own `evidence` array (G1b, enforced by scripts/validate_conflict_resolution.py -- not expressible as a plain JSON Schema cross-field constraint).

disposition_of_other.description: The losing evidence's semantic_disposition after resolution -- same vocabulary as evidence-schema.json's own semantic_disposition.
